All media is biased. It does not matter if there is one company, or ten billion - each will have their angle, and neither situation is preferable: in the case of one, you will almost assuredly have manipulation of one sort or another happening, and in the case of ten billion, there will be so much fragmentation and focus that these businesses would focus on one topic or individual or what-have-you and individuals who felt strongly about that topic would go there for all their news, making them easily manipulated even by accident, though it would almost assuredly happen purposefully after awhile.

We know that media is biased. Intelligent free-thinking citizens still have political discourse with each other; people who are concerned can read and pore through multiple sources, acquiring a more thorough picture of the whole even if it is presented in a fragmented manner. The internet also exists, and through this channel you can find out about all sorts of things that the "media" may not be covering properly or wants to hide.

The only reason I can see this being a concern is the impact it has on our politics, which... well, I guess there's one more reason we can throw onto the pile of "why TZ is a monarchist." If people were actually concerned about this, then those who have studied their history know the one sure-fire way to resolve it, though I don't blame them for not wanting to pursue it.

The idea is not to cleanse all bias. The idea is to gain more different views. The fewer the owners, the fewer the viewpoints.
